My answer is D, about 75%. The team note is wrong: China and India were still low-income countries in 1997, not upper-middle income, and together they hold roughly a third of the world's people. So the low and lower-middle income groups made up most of the world's population, which fits about 75%.

I'm working from memory of the World Bank figures, not a lookup, and the $1230 cutoff doesn't match the Bank's standard thresholds as I recall them.

CONFIDENCE: 66
